result.question: Compare R&D spending as a share of revenue across Tesla, Apple, and Nvidia in their most recent fiscal years.
result.answer:
R&D spending as a share of revenue in each company's most recent fiscal year was as follows.

Tesla (FY 2025, ended December 31, 2025) reported R&D expenses of $6,411 million on revenue of $94,827 million, yielding an R&D-to-revenue ratio of approximately 6.8% [xbrl:0001628280-26-003952:us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense:2025-12-31] [xbrl:0001628280-26-003952:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-12-31].

Apple (FY 2025, ended September 27, 2025) reported R&D expenses of $34,550 million on total net sales of $416,161 million, yielding an R&D-to-revenue ratio of approximately 8.3% [xbrl:0000320193-25-000079:us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense:2025-09-27] [xbrl:0000320193-25-000079:us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax:2025-09-27] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8-p001].

Nvidia (FY 2026, ended January 25, 2026) reported R&D expenses of $18,497 million on revenue of $215,938 million, yielding an R&D-to-revenue ratio of approximately 8.6% [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense:2026-01-25] [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25].

Among the three companies, Nvidia had the highest R&D-to-revenue ratio at approximately 8.6%, followed closely by Apple at approximately 8.3%, with Tesla the lowest at approximately 6.8% [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense:2026-01-25] [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25] [xbrl:0000320193-25-000079:us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense:2025-09-27] [xbrl:0000320193-25-000079:us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax:2025-09-27] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8-p001] [xbrl:0001628280-26-003952:us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense:2025-12-31] [xbrl:0001628280-26-003952:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-12-31].

The following claims could not be verified against their cited sources and were removed from the answer:
- In absolute dollar terms, Apple's R&D expense of $34,550 million exceeded both Nvidia's $18,497 million and Tesla's $6,411 million.
